doc.name: A — tableware catalogue, chrome podium, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: reactive-glaze dinner plate stack
Category: tableware
Shot programme: chrome podium
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a tableware catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the dead-on front elevation in a chrome podium treatment.

SUBJECT. A reactive-glaze dinner plate stack. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Straight-on front elevation, lens at exact label centre, zero perspective distortion. Shoot on a 24mm wide at f/2.8, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a single 90cm softbox key at 45 degrees with a white bounce card for fill. Stage the product on or against crushed velvet, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a bleach-bypass look with crushed saturation and lifted contrast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
